newsitem.title: GREECE: NEW DEMOCRACY PARTY CALLS OFF ATHENS RALLY - EVERT.
newsitem.headline: NEW DEMOCRACY PARTY CALLS OFF ATHENS RALLY - EVERT.

text.p: Conservative New Democracy party leader Miltiadis Evert called off Thursday's planned mass rally in Athens, traditionally held at the end of national election campaigns, and said he would hold a news conference instead.
Evert had called on socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis to face him in a second televised election debate on that night but the ruling socialists have declined.

Simitis and Evert faced off on television last Friday, in a debate held under strict conditions imposed largely by Simitis. Many analysts called it a draw -- with no winning punches and no major gaffs by either candidate -- and polls taken in the Athens region showed Simitis scoring a close win.
Evert said he had also called on the four smaller parties in the race for Sunday's elections to join in a televised debate next Thursday.
He said only Nikos Constantopoulos of the Leftist Coalition party had agreed to participate. The others had said there was little point in such a debate if Simitis refused to attend.
Opinion polls have shown widespread voter indifference to the coming election, which Simitis called a year early in anticipation of a landslide victory.

Poll experts have said the two major parties were in an unexpectedly close race, with around 31 percent each, but they have noted that Simitis has the advantage because of the large block of centre-left votes he can try to woo from the smaller parties.
Political analysts have said for several days that Evert might call off the Athens rally.

They said a mass rally in Athens might prompt centre-left voters in the smaller parties to shift to the socialist party for fear of a conservative victory. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
